title: Coordinate Kummer boundary under arbitrary geometric pullback
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, assume $e=e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$, and put $N=n/e\geq1$ and $m=\ell^N$, so $mA=0$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. In the affine-line datum [def-pur-affine-line-datum] write $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $s:Y\hookrightarrow X$ for the zero section, $U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}$ for its complement, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and $F=A_X(1)$. The coefficient comparison is $\theta_T:A_T(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{m,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A$, and $\varphi_T(u)=\theta_T^{-1}(u\otimes1_A)$.

Use the support boundary [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] and the supported-Hom identifications [lem-pur-supported-hom, lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback]. Let $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed; no finite-type hypothesis on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ over $k$ is imposed. Write $X'=\mathbf A^1_\Omega$, $U'=\mathbf G_{m,\Omega}$, $s':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\hookrightarrow X'$, and $h:X'\to X$, $h_U:U'\to U$ for the induced maps, with $t'=h^*t$ and $F'=h^*F$. On the etale site define
$$\kappa_{A,\mathrm{et}}(t')=H^1(u\mapsto u\otimes1_A)(\delta_{m,U'}(t'))\in H^1(U',\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,U'}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A),$$
where $\delta_m$ is the ordinary Kummer connecting map of the datum. Its pro-etale comparison image, read through $\theta_{U'}$, is denoted $\kappa(t')$. The exponent $m$ and coefficient map are unchanged by this pullback. Put $\alpha=\partial\kappa(t)$, $\alpha'=\partial'\kappa(t')$, and $M=\chi_{s,F}^2(\alpha):s_*A_Y\to F[2]$. With $c:h^*s_*A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}s'_*A_\Omega$ the canonical supported-constant comparison, the following simultaneous equalities hold:
$$h_U^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(t'),\qquad h^*\alpha=\alpha',\qquad \chi_{s',F'}^2(\alpha')=h^*M\circ c^{-1}.$$
These are identities on the ordinary etale models and, with the canonical twist, shift and supported-constant comparisons, on their small pro-etale images. In particular the support pullback is the coordinate boundary formed with the same coefficient extension, not just some generator of its group.

proof.text: Over an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the image of $g$, the base-changed polynomial and Laurent polynomial rings are $\Omega\otimes_R R[t]=\Omega[t]$ and $\Omega\otimes_R R[t,t^{-1}]=\Omega[t,t^{-1}]$. The quotient $R[t]/(t)=R$ pulls back to $\Omega[t]/(t)=\Omega$. Thus the zero sections and their open complements form the required Cartesian squares, and the coordinate is exactly $t\mapsto t'$. These identities use the explicit geometry in [def-pur-affine-line-datum] and do not require $\Omega$ to be finite type over $k$.

source.place: Geometric-fibre sentence; explicit coordinate-ring verification of its Cartesian zero-section square.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-relative-kummer-coefficient-normalization] to $h_U:U'\to U$, with $r=m=\ell^N$ and the unit $t$. Its hypotheses hold: $e\mid n$ gives a finite free $\mathbf Z/m$-algebra $A$, and $m$ is invertible on all $k$-schemes. Its naturality formula gives $h_U^*\kappa_{U,A}(t)=\kappa_{U',A}(t')$ on the etale site. Here the same coefficient morphism is used: in its compatible root coordinates $\zeta^a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, $u\mapsto u\otimes1_A$ remains $\zeta^a\mapsto a1_A$ after pullback. Neither $m$ nor $1_A$ changes. Apply [lem-pur-relative-kummer-site-normalization] to identify these precise etale classes with the datum's pro-etale classes through $\theta$, and to obtain the same equality under pro-etale pullback. Both cited statements allow every $k$-morphism, including this $g$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, label lemma-kummer-sequence; coefficient and site normalization supplied by the cited nodes, with the pure-tensor calculation written here.

proof.text: Use [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] for the two pairs $(X,s(Y))$ and $(X',s'(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega))$, and their map $h$ from step 1. Its functoriality in the pair and coefficients gives $h^*\circ\partial=\partial'\circ h_U^*$. Consequently $h^*\alpha=h^*\partial\kappa(t)=\partial' h_U^*\kappa(t)=\partial'\kappa(t')=\alpha'$. This applies on both sites: $F$ is a finite torsion sheaf and the theorem explicitly includes the pro-etale finite-torsion case. The boundary is the one in the datum throughout.

source.place: Theorem 9.4, pp. 65-67; functorial Ext construction of the localization boundary; pro-etale refinement as stated in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] with $i=s$, $i'=s'$, $a=2$ and the sheaf $F$ in degree zero. Step 1 supplies its Cartesian square, and it requires no finiteness of $h$ or $X'$. Its formula and step 3 give $\chi_{s',F'}^2(\alpha')=\chi_{s',F'}^2(h^*\alpha)=h^*(\chi_{s,F}^2(\alpha))\circ c^{-1}=h^*M\circ c^{-1}$. The same node explicitly identifies the etale and pro-etale supported-Hom maps through exact site inverse image, shift comparison and the canonical supported-constant comparison, compatibly with $h^*$ and $c$. Therefore these are the specified representatives on both sites. Combined with step 2, the pulled-back class is the coordinate boundary with its original coefficient map.
